citations.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI inference
excerpts: # Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI inference
Reyna Abhyankar, Dylan Lim, and Simran Arora
- 40+ Models Chosen for Production...40+ Models Chosen for Production...40+ Models Chosen for Production...

AI inference workloads are dynamic. There are thousands of regimes spanning new models, hardware platforms, customers, use cases, and traffic shapes. It’s no longer scalable to optimize each of these regimes by hand.

- Architectures are highly variable: it’s been \~11 years since the Transformer. We might have thought there would be more consolidation, but none of the top-10 open-source LLMs on OpenRouter use the same architecture!

- Workloads are highly variable: Together serves many trillions of tokens per day across thousands of customers, each with a different traffic shape (batch size, sequence length, MoE expert imbalance, attention sparsity, session duration, domain).
- Hardware is highly variable: H100s, B200s, B300s, NVL72, VR, Groq, and more each require distinct strategies.

Agents are a great fit for this problem, in theory. They can adapt to new workloads and search over the space of possible optimizations without relying on fixed rules or heuristics that plague human experts and traditional machine learning compilers. However, today’s agentic systems are bottlenecked by the speed of experimentation.
### **We introduce Together Compiler (TKCC), the first *truly* *continual* optimization loop that leverages high-throughput agents to optimize to diverse inference workloads**

citations.title: Benchmarking inference at scale: coding agents
excerpts: # Benchmarking inference at scale: coding agents

![Bar chart titled Coding agents with pink and orange bars on dark background with code snippets behind.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69654e88dce9154b5f12070c/6a0cb006d887ece070f3a7e4_20260501_Blog_Series_Code_Agents.jpg)
Alex Angus, Will Van Eaton, Dan Fu
- 40+ Models Chosen for Production...40+ Models Chosen for Production...40+ Models Chosen for Production...

On a production coding agent workload, Together Inference Engine delivers **31% more TPS than the next fastest OSS engine** on the same hardware, and maintains 2× better TTFT at saturation. The gains come from full-stack optimization: ThunderMLA, custom kernel rewrites, and end-to-end profiling on real traffic.
Most inference benchmarks measure a single user hitting a dedicated endpoint. The numbers look great. They're also useless for reasoning about production.

In production, you're running dozens or hundreds of concurrent requests. They compete for the same KV cache, the same memory bandwidth, the same GPU cycles. What matters is what happens to every user when the system is under load.
We built this benchmark to answer that question for coding agents. It's a workload that hits inference hard: long inputs, high concurrency, and no tolerance for latency degradation under load.

citations.title: Privacy and security
excerpts: Some models are offered as *passthrough*, which means Together forwards your prompts and responses directly to the upstream provider. The provider handles that data under its own data policy.

The **Passthrough models** toggle in [organization privacy settings](#organization-privacy-settings) controls whether your organization can use these models, independent of the training opt-in. To keep all traffic on Together's infrastructure, turn it off. Non-passthrough models keep working as normal.
## Enterprise data residency and private networking

For select serverless models, [geo-specific inference](https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/geo-specific-inference.md) keeps inference processing in the United States, with no GPUs to provision. The guarantee applies to requests sent to `us-api.together.ai`. It covers only where those requests are processed, not where data is stored, logged, or routed.

For other data-residency, regulatory, or compliance requirements, such as GDPR, Together supports private networking and virtual private cloud (VPC) deployments, including in EU regions. Use a [dedicated endpoint](https://docs.together.ai/docs/dedicated-endpoints/overview.md), or [contact sales](https://www.together.ai/contact-sales) to discuss the right setup for your workload.

Together AI accepts security vulnerability reports through its [HackerOne program](https://hackerone.com/together_ai). The program is private, so viewing it and submitting reports requires a HackerOne account. Program details are published in the standard [security.txt](https://together.ai/.well-known/security.txt) file. If you believe you've found a security issue, submit it through HackerOne rather than a support ticket.

Models published by third-party authors (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, etc.) and hosted on Together run on Together's own infrastructure. They do not call out to the model author. The model author has no access to your requests or API calls.
For example, DeepSeek models are hosted in Together's secure North America data centers. DeepSeek itself receives no user requests or API traffic from this deployment.
Models on Together are hosted at full precision. Together does not distill them, force system prompts, or layer censorship on top. The version you call is the version the model author published.
